title: Changing event image randomly without using event pages

posts.author: cuby
posts.body:
Before I spend a huge amount of time on this that might all end up for naught, I wanted to get some advice on how to go about this problem. No existing threads specifically address this.
In my project, there are events strewn throughout the map that are "garbage". The player can pick up the garbage, naturally.
I have 16 different little garbage images, and I'd like the garbage events to randomly choose an image from among them when the map loads.
The garbage images are in the B Tileset.
My first thought was to create a common event that would set a variable randomly to 1-16, and then I would use Set Movement Route to set the garbage image.
However, movement route doesn't permit me to select from a Tileset image, unfortunately.
The only other solution I can figure is for each and every garbage event to be an autorun with 16 event pages, and for the first event page to set one of 16 switches to on, which would run the corresponding page and then turn that activating switch off before the engine goes on to run the subsequent garbage events.
This solution is not only time-consuming but it also feels quite nauseating from a basic coding hygiene perspective -- there has to be an easier way.
If anyone has any thoughts, I'm all ears! Thank you!!

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
Just make the garbage a character graphic instead of being on the tileset.
If you wanted to do the second option though, you don't have to use switches. You could just use a variable for each piece of garbage. You'd still have 16 pages, though.

If you are using a common event, be sure to reference the correct event ID - I will use ID 1 for this example.
Character Directions and Patterns for single spritesheet:
Code:
Down  (2): 0 1 2
Left  (4): 0 1 2
Right (6): 0 1 2
Up    (8): 0 1 2
Here is the script call you must use to target a specific cell (assuming you are in a common event and not using move route commands) - for direction right, pattern 2:
JavaScript:
$gameMap.event(1).setDirection(6);
$gameMap.event(1)._originalPattern = 2;
Do note that these need to be in the same script call and not two separate calls because the engine will run them separately and you will notice two changes, one right after the other, instead of just one change using one call.
If you are interested in the alternative, I'll be more than happy to post the code for loading targeted events with notetag, Tileset B usage with randomized placement on the map upon loading and randomized Tileset B images which are static and do not require direction or pattern changes. I use it for picking up plants in my game as a fun little mini-game (will probably be timed). It's a lot cleaner with just a few lines of code. I'll be sure to put notes in as well as a reference.

Tileset B (indexes 0-255) with 16 "garbage" events, Harold (event 17) as parallel event to control everything, and 8 treasure chests that do nothing so that you can see that the script only targets the events with the note tag <garbage>:
Event 1-16 - Page 1: Note <garbage> with Common Event "Get Garbage".
- Priority: Same as characters
- Trigger: Player Touch
- No image set
Events 1-16 - Page 2: Self Switch A checked on
- Priority: Below characters
- Trigger: Action Button
- No image set
Harold Event 17 - Page 1: script and comments in image
- Priority: Same as characters
- Trigger: Parallel
Script Code for convenience:
JavaScript:
const eventId = $dataMap.events.reduce((acc, cur) => {
  if (cur?.meta.garbage) acc.push(cur.id);
  return acc}, []);
for (const id of eventId) {
  this.character(id).setTileImage( Math.randomInt(49) + 8 );
};
$gameVariables.setValue(1, eventId);
Math.randomInt(49) function generates a random number between 0 and the number you specify (in this case, the numbers range from 0-48). Adding 8 to it allows the number to always start no lower than 48 so it essentially becomes 48-56.
Harold Event 17 - Page 2: Self Switch A is checked on
Pretty much the same info with a few additions to reset the self switches of the <garbage> events and reset/randomize the tileset images of those events.
- Priority: Same as characters
- Trigger: Action Button
Script Call:
JavaScript:
const gSS = $gameSelfSwitches;
for (const key in gSS._data) {
  if ( key.split(',')[0] == this._mapId &&
       $gameVariables.value(1).includes(Number(key.split(',')[1])) )
       gSS.setValue(key, false);
};
JavaScript:
for (const id of $gameVariables.value(1)) {
  this.character(id).setTileImage( Math.randomInt(41) + 8 );
};
Edit: I used 49 in the first page but 41 here, feel free to use the values you need - here, the range becomes 40-48)
Treasure Chest Events 18-25: Image set to Treasure. Just a placeholder event.
Common Event "Get Garbage":
Play SE Book1
Add Items to Inventory (Garbage is set to Key Item to separate it from normal inventory)
Control Self Switch A = ON allows each individual event to use their own selfswitch when it runs this common event.
Hope this is what you were looking for! You will have to customize as needed but this is pretty much the workflow if you are going this way and wanting to simplify.
The issue, as with all evals, is that error detecting and console errors are not helpful so you really need to know where and how to approach this and deduce your way through possible errors. Otherwise, you are welcome to use these calls and work through them.

Awesome! That's good to know that passability also affects the event since it is utilizing the tile ID - I will make note of that.
Math.randomInt(8) + 40 basically means "Randomly choose from 8 integers (0-7) and add 40 to it", making the range 40-47.
Correct! Math.randomInt(16) + 40 is "randomly choose from 16 integers (0-15) and add 40 to it", making the range 40-55.
You are welcome and I'm glad it worked out for you!
When working with the engine, always approach it with the event commands first until you know that a script call or a plugin would be more efficient or is needed. As you have already experienced, debugging took the longest, but you also learn a lot about the engine as well. Basically, event commands are RTP/preloaded script calls to the corescripts of the engine), script calls are custom event commands, and plugin commands are simple to read/write (depending on the plugin)
syntax that calls a custom group of functions and makes them work together to extend the system (as defined by the plugin).
Seeing that this mechanic would have needed several pages of event commands, variables, conditions, etc. (which would have been harder to set up since it was unable to use some of the powerful functions like filter/reduce/for-of without a script call), it was better (at least from my perspective currently) to create a script call for it (really, only a couple of lines when you think about it).
